chunks: Indeed, when the believer shaves his head at Minā and then buries it, he will come on the Day of Resurrection, and every hair will have an eloquent tongue proclaiming the talbiyah in the name of its owner.

key_terms.اَلْمُؤْمِنَ: the believing person whose act is being described
key_terms.بِمِنًى: at Minā, the sacred hajj location where the shaving takes place
key_terms.تُلَبِّي: it recites the talbiyah, the pilgrim’s response to Allah during hajj
key_terms.شَعْرَةٍ: each individual hair that will testify
key_terms.لِسَانٌ طَلْقٌ: an eloquent tongue, meaning a clear mode of testimony or proclamation
key_terms.يَوْمَ اَلْقِيَامَةِ: the Day of Resurrection when deeds and signs of devotion appear

ai.seo_question: What is the virtue of burying one’s hair after shaving at Minā during hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith describes the spiritual merit of shaving the head at Minā and burying the hair during hajj. It portrays this act as bearing witness for the believer on the Day of Resurrection, with every hair proclaiming the talbiyah on behalf of its owner.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.2198 - Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) said:
"When a believer shaves their head at Mina and buries the hair, they will come on the Day of Judgment, and every hair will have a fluent tongue calling out the Talbiyah in the name of its owner."
